primary_claim: Linear safety probes that successfully detect (AUROC≥0.91) and steer a feature often fail to 'silence' it via causal projection, showing that detect/steer success is not evidence of a true causal handle; a calibration-time cosine diagnostic between plain and within-class-whitened difference-of-means directions predicts silencing success across 4-5 model families and 2 features, recovering all 17 existing causal handles and correctly alarming on the remaining 5 in a 22-cell battery.

effect.metric: necessity-check protocol recovery of true causal handles vs. correct alarms, 22-cell battery
effect.value: recovers all 17 causal handles that exist and correctly alarms on the remaining 5

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies the implicit norm in prior probe-steering work (Representation Engineering, ActAdd, Inference-Time Intervention) of validating a direction via 'extract + steer = done' -- a sufficiency check, not a necessity check -- showing this leaves silent failures where the probe reads a confound rather than the causal axis
Provides controlled empirical evidence for a qualitative concern raised in the Claude Mythos Preview System Card that the causal effects of individual features change over the course of post-training
stated_future_work: Observe how the detect/steer/silence dissociation evolves when the model is actively adversarial to feature detection and steering
limitations_stated: Four families, two features tested; not enough to predict from pretraining metadata alone which regime a novel family falls into
Projective ablation can self-repair: other layers or components could reconstitute the removed signal downstream
Linear only; characterizes calibration-time dissociation but not arbitrary training dynamics, and may not hold for SAEs
The 0.80 cosine threshold was fit on the collected data; transfer to features other than refusal and sycophancy is the claim the author is least confident in
quote: Probe accuracy is not evidence of a causal handle.
